sections.heading: C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
A court report that a driver has not met a traffic citation's terms can trigger a Non-Resident Violator Compact suspension for either Wyoming or other-state citations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
In a Non-Resident Violator Compact case, the licensing state takes suspension action rather than the state where the violation happened. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
The citation-related suspension continues until the court supplies satisfaction notice and the reinstatement fee is paid. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A01
Limited privileges are unavailable for the Non-Resident Violator Compact suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A01
Before the citation-related suspension starts, court notice that the citation requirements are satisfied causes deletion of the suspension from the record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A01
After the citation-related suspension starts, reinstatement requires both the court's satisfaction notice and the reinstatement fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
A fourth moving-violation conviction within a 12-month period triggers notice of a 90-day suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A01
Each additional moving violation within the 12-month period produces another 90-day suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A01
Moving-violation lookbacks use the offense date rather than a later conviction date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A01
A moving violation involves control or lack of control while the vehicle is moving and results in conviction, including conviction for violating a license restriction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A02
A court conviction for lacking liability insurance triggers the compulsory-insurance suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A02
A compulsory-insurance suspension lasts until an SR-22 insurance form is filed with the department. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A02
Limited privileges are unavailable for a compulsory-insurance suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A02
Filing an SR-22 before a compulsory-insurance suspension starts removes that suspension from the record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A02
After a compulsory-insurance suspension starts, reinstatement requires an SR-22 filing and the reinstatement fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A02
Displaying or using another person's license or ID card can lead to unlawful-use suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A02
Possessing an altered or tampered-with license or ID card can trigger unlawful-use suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A02
Lending a license or ID card for another person to use as identification is unlawful. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A02
Knowingly supplying false statements, fictitious information or a false name, or concealing a fact, is unlawful on a license or ID application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A02
Using another person's name, address, Social Security number or birth date on a license or ID application is unlawful. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

sections.heading: C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
FACT_ID: sec04-R21 | anchor: A02
The listed license or ID misuse can result in card cancellation, a 90-day suspension for the person using or lending it, or both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R22 | anchor: A02
A DFS notice that child-support arrears of at least $5,000 have persisted for 90 consecutive days triggers child-support suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R23 | anchor: A03
Ending a child-support suspension requires DFS notification of full compliance or an approved payment plan, together with payment of the reinstatement fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R24 | anchor: A03
A moving-violation conviction committed while holding a restricted Class RC license causes a 90-day suspension for the first offense. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R25 | anchor: A03
A second or later moving-violation conviction while holding that restricted Class RC license causes a one-year suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R26 | anchor: A03
Violating an intermediate-license restriction causes a 30-day suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R27 | anchor: A03
For a driver under 21, driving while privileges are suspended, revoked or canceled causes a further 30-day suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R28 | anchor: A03
An uninsured-accident suspension results when the driver's insurance cannot be verified at the time of the crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R29 | anchor: A03
An uninsured driver may submit the other crash parties' notarized release stating that they do not hold the driver liable for damage or injury, or that restitution has been made. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R30 | anchor: A03
Another uninsured-crash option is a conditional release signed and notarized by the driver and the other parties stating an agreement to pay for damage or injury. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R31 | anchor: A03
An uninsured driver may instead post a cash deposit covering total property damage plus $25,000 for each injury. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R32 | anchor: A03
The uninsured-crash cash deposit may be refunded one year after the crash only if there are no judgments against the driver. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R33 | anchor: A03
An uninsured driver unable to provide the listed release or deposit options may submit a signed, notarized affidavit one year after the crash stating that no resulting judgments remain unsatisfied. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-R34 | anchor: A04
A driver suspended after the uninsured-crash process must also pay the reinstatement fee and file an SR-22 in addition to satisfying a listed crash-resolution option. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R35 | anchor: A04
An otherwise eligible suspended driver may request a Record Review for possible issuance of a probationary license allowing limited privileges. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R36 | anchor: A04
A Record Review request must be in writing with the required fee, and both must be postmarked within 20 days of the notice date. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R37 | anchor: A04
A driver can receive only one probationary license during a five-year period. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R38 | anchor: A04
A Contested Case Hearing request must be written, include the required fee and be postmarked within 20 days of the notice date. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R39 | anchor: A04
Revocation cancels the driver license, and relicensing after revocation ends requires a driver investigation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R40 | anchor: A04
A third or later DWUI is listed as a revocation-causing offense. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

sections.heading: C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Suspensions, revocations and reinstatement
FACT_ID: sec04-R41 | anchor: A04
A third or later reckless-driving offense is listed as a cause of revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R42 | anchor: A04
Leaving an injury-crash scene is listed as a revocation-causing offense. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R43 | anchor: A04
Homicide by vehicle is listed as an offense causing revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R44 | anchor: A04
A felony directly resulting from the manner of driving is listed as a cause of revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R45 | anchor: A04
An SR-22 is an insurance certificate that the insurer files with the department. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R46 | anchor: A05
The financial-responsibility proof period stated for covered violations or actions is three years beginning when proof is required. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R47 | anchor: A05
When an SR-22 is on file, the insurer must notify the department if the insurance is canceled. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R48 | anchor: A05
If the required SR-22 is missing when a mandatory suspension ends, driving privileges remain suspended until it is filed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R49 | anchor: A05
A suspension or revocation generally starts 30 days after the department mails the order or law enforcement gives it to the driver, or after existing suspensions end. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R50 | anchor: A05
Required ignition-interlock installation is at the applicant's expense. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R51 | anchor: A05
The device summary requires six months of interlock for a first DWUI conviction or deferred prosecution when the administrative action shows BAC at least 0.15 percent. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R52 | anchor: A05
The device summary requires one year of interlock after a second DWUI conviction involving alcohol. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R53 | anchor: A05
The device summary gives a lifetime interlock requirement for a fourth or later alcohol-related DWUI conviction, with a possible removal petition five years after conviction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R54 | anchor: A05
A driver convicted of an alcohol-related offense requiring interlock must file an SR-22. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R55 | anchor: A06
A driver subject to the interlock-license installation requirements must use a department-certified technician at a certified installation site for every vehicle driven. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R56 | anchor: A06
For an IIR restricted driver license, the driver must bring the document labeled lease agreement/certification of installation to the local driver-examination office. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R57 | anchor: A06
An interlock-restricted license cannot be issued if driving privileges are suspended, revoked or canceled in any state for a reason other than the DWUI conviction creating the interlock requirement. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R58 | anchor: A06
The interlock-license applicant must take and pass any required licensing tests. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R59 | anchor: A06
Another license type is unavailable until the driver has held the interlock-restricted license for the required period. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R60 | anchor: A06
A court order directing participation in the 24/7 Sobriety Program instead of interlock allows the driver to apply for a 24/7 restricted license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]
